sections.h2: How is Maryland laid out for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Maryland has 23 counties plus the independent city of Baltimore, and the capital is Annapolis. Wikipedia puts the 2025 population estimate at 6,265,347, which makes it the 19th-largest state, and it describes four broad regions that feel quite different to a seller.

  • Central Maryland is the densest area, built around Baltimore and the Washington, D.C. suburbs.
  • Southern Maryland is still somewhat rural but has suburbanized since the 1960s, with Waldorf, Prince Frederick, California and Lexington Park as population centers.
  • The Eastern Shore is lower, flatter and more rural, east of the Chesapeake Bay, with Salisbury and Ocean City among its key cities.
  • Western Maryland is mountainous, with Allegany and Garrett as the westernmost counties.

The Chesapeake Bay nearly splits the state in two. Sixteen counties and Baltimore border its tidal waters, with more than 4,000 miles of shoreline, so waterfront and flood questions come up in more places than many sellers expect.

sections.h2: Which Maryland counties are the largest?
sections.html:
Montgomery County is the largest, followed by Prince George's County and Baltimore County. The 2020 census counts below come from the Wikipedia county list, and the same page shows Kent County as the smallest at 19,198.

County seats matter when you need a court or land records office. Rockville serves Montgomery County, Upper Marlboro serves Prince George's, Towson serves Baltimore County, Annapolis serves Anne Arundel, Ellicott City serves Howard, Frederick serves its own county and Bel Air serves Harford.

sections.h2: What does Maryland's economy and climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
Government, defense and health care anchor much of the economy, and the weather is varied enough that the load on a roof and a heating system differs between the coast and the mountains. Wikipedia lists manufacturing, retail, public administration, real estate, higher education, IT, defense contracting, health care and biotechnology among the main sectors. Fort Meade hosts the Defense Information Systems Agency, U.S. Cyber Command and the National Security Agency.

The same source puts the median household income at $98,700 in 2023, third-highest in the country, and says Montgomery County produces about 25 percent of the state's GDP.

On climate, the eastern half has hot, humid summers and cool to cold winters. In the Piedmont, snowfall usually exceeds 20 inches and temperatures below 10 degrees Fahrenheit are not rare. The western mountains can see more than 100 inches of snow. Annual rainfall runs about 35 to 45 inches, there are roughly 30 to 40 thunderstorm days and about six tornadoes a year, and the state is somewhat vulnerable to tropical cyclones.

sections.h2: How is property tax run in Maryland?
sections.html:
The state appraises and the local governments bill. The Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation, known as SDAT, estimates fair market value and certifies assessments to local governments, which turn them into bills by applying their tax rates. Property tax is primarily a local revenue source.

  • SDAT must appraise each of its more than two million property accounts once every three years.
  • There are 24 local assessment offices, one for each county and one for Baltimore City.
  • An owner who thinks the market value on a notice is wrong can file a Petition for Review or New Owner Appeal online, and SDAT charges no fee for the appeal or for the assessment worksheet.

The homestead credit limits how fast a principal residence's taxable assessment can rise. Every county and municipality must cap increases at 10 percent a year or less, and local governments can pick a lower figure. The owner applies once, buyers are mailed an application after the deed is recorded, and the home must be lived in for at least six months of the year including July 1. The credit generally does not carry over when ownership changes.

sections.h2: What transfer and recording taxes apply when a Maryland house sells?
sections.html:
The state transfer tax is 0.5 percent of the consideration, and counties set their own recordation tax. Tax-Property § 13-203 sets the 0.5 percent rate, and it falls to 0.25 percent for a first-time Maryland home buyer who will live in the house, with the seller paying the entire tax at that reduced rate.

Recordation tax works differently. Under § 12-103, each county's governing body and the Baltimore City council may set the rate, and it applies to each $500 or fraction of consideration. A local government may exempt part of the consideration for an owner-occupied home when the buyer will live there at least 7 months of a 12-month period, and may also exempt a first-time buyer who signs a sworn statement. Instruments are recorded with the clerk of the circuit court for the county.

sections.h2: How do probate and inherited property work across Maryland?
sections.html:
Each county has a Register of Wills, and nobody can dispose of estate assets until a personal representative is appointed. The Register's administration pamphlet describes small estates as $50,000 or less in probate assets, or $100,000 if the spouse is sole heir or legatee, and says an inventory is due within three months of appointment.

Two death taxes sit on top of this. The inheritance tax is 10 percent of the clear value of property going to people outside the exempt family list, and the estate tax exclusion is $5,000,000 for a death in 2019 or later. Our Maryland estate tax guide goes through both, and the Register of Wills page explains how the tax is billed and collected.

sections.h2: Where do foreclosure and landlord disputes go?
sections.html:
Foreclosures go to the circuit courts, and landlord and tenant cases go to the District Court. According to the Maryland Courts housing page, a lender may file for foreclosure 90 days after default and must send a Notice of Intent 45 days before filing. Owner-occupied primary residences can request foreclosure mediation for a $50 non-refundable fee, which a judge may waive or reduce.

  • A borrower has 45 days after service to pay or defend before a sale can occur.
  • Sale notices run at least three weeks, and the sale date is announced at least 10 days ahead.
  • An owner can redeem by paying the full amount up to one business day before the sale.
  • Tenants in a foreclosed home get notices 45 days before the sale and again 10 to 30 days before.

For rentals with three or fewer units, a tenant of six months or more generally gets a chance to offer before the owner lists the home, under Real Property § 8-119, with exceptions for foreclosure, estate and family transfers.

sections.h2: How should a seller use the Maryland guides below?
sections.html:
Start with the guide that matches the problem in front of you. The city and county pages cover local facts, the statewide pages cover rules that apply everywhere, and the right entry point depends on what is driving the sale.

  • An inherited house usually points to the probate and estate tax pages.
  • A tenant problem points to the eviction notice and process pages.
  • A tax bill or assessment question points to the property tax pages for the county.
  • A missed mortgage payment points to the foreclosure and tax sale pages.

faqs.q: How many counties does Maryland have?
faqs.a: Maryland has 23 counties plus Baltimore City, which is treated separately from the counties. SDAT runs 24 local assessment offices, one for each of those jurisdictions.

faqs.q: Who sets property tax rates in Maryland?
faqs.a: Local governments do. SDAT estimates market value and certifies assessments, and county and city governments apply their rates to produce the bills.

faqs.q: How often are Maryland properties reassessed?
faqs.a: SDAT must appraise each property account once every three years. An owner can appeal an assessment online at no charge.

faqs.q: What is the Maryland state transfer tax?
faqs.a: It is 0.5 percent of the consideration under Tax-Property § 13-203. For a first-time Maryland buyer who will live in the home, the rate is 0.25 percent and the seller pays all of it.

faqs.q: Who sets the Maryland recordation tax?
faqs.a: Each county's governing body, and the city council in Baltimore, sets its own rate on each $500 of consideration, and deeds are recorded with the clerk of the circuit court.

faqs.q: When can a Maryland lender file for foreclosure?
faqs.a: A lender may file 90 days after default and must send a Notice of Intent 45 days before filing, according to the Maryland Courts housing page.
